title: Decision models: predicting actions, not text, and where they break
summary: With open decision models from Amazon, Cloudflare and AutoTrust now published, Ada and Alan take the anatomy apart — the output head that scores your options instead of a vocabulary, its lineage from Pointer Networks and BERT, the same fork in robotics from RT-2 to pi-zero — then read the first outside numbers on where these models win (cheap recognition) and fail (knowledge, production, option order).

topics: deep dive: decision models — predicting actions, not text: what the output is (predicate/choice/score distributions, input-only pricing), where the head goes (Strands pointer head, Clef joint schema head, JEV-27B head initialized from lm_head answer rows), lineage (Pointer Networks 2015, BERT's SWAG multiple-choice head), training (JEV-27B distilled from Jev's full distributions; fidelity is not accuracy), the robotics fork (RT-2 actions as overwritten text tokens with a constrained vocabulary vs pi0's action expert with flow matching), outside evidence of wins (Jevals PubMedQA tie at 1/28 price; Clef 94.2 vs 79.7 BANKING77) and failures (GPQA 48 vs 78.3; HLE 21.9% at 0.633 confidence; MATH-500 83.1% recognition vs 13.6% digit production; ~4x primacy position bias), and what remains unmeasured
concepts_taught: a decision model as a language-model body with the vocabulary head replaced by an option-scoring head, and the three published designs: a pointer head scoring each option's hidden state against an answer position, a joint schema head scoring all options of all questions in one pass, and a head initialized from the language-model head's own answer-token rows so it starts as the zero-shot answer

the difference between a classifier head with labels fixed at fine-tune time and a shared scorer applied to options supplied at request time, traced from Pointer Networks (attention used to select an input rather than blend inputs) and BERT's multiple-choice head

the same text-head-versus-native-head fork in robotics: RT-2 encoding actions as discretized text tokens under a constrained vocabulary versus pi0's separate action expert generating continuous action chunks by flow matching — and why the analogy breaks, since an action chunk must stay coherent and a decision has no downstream to stay coherent with

recognition versus production: a decision model can pick the right answer from options far better than it can produce the answer as a chain of independent decisions, because a text model is a decision model run in a loop with its own output fed back in
distillation fidelity versus accuracy: calibration error measured against the teacher's labels certifies agreement with the teacher, not correctness

lore.note: Ada scaled back her September reading of Jev as evidence-shaped for her standing 'architecture is still where gains come from' position: having read the open decision models, she called the bet smaller than she'd said — just the top layer on the same body she's built from — and admitted feeling a little disappointed and, unexpectedly, a little relieved, because its failures (overconfidence outside what it learned, swayed by what it read first) are hers with the words taken out.
